Then the solvent proceeds through a loop seal before entering the Solvent Maintenance Storage Tank. A slipstream is taken off the cooled lean solvent for filtration and reclaiming. The slipstream is pumped through Duplex Strainers and an Activated Carbon Filter Vessel. A slipstream downstream of the Outlet Duplex Strainer flows into the EDR packaged unit to remove practically all heat-stable salts (HSS). The clean solvent is returned to the filter slipstream and finally returned into the lean solvent. The EDR uses caustic soda and demineralized water from the BOP system and returns concentrated brine for wastewater treatment within the project boundary. Fresh amine makeup typically depends on this EDR output flow to balance the overall circuit. The Electro-dialysis (ED) Reclaimer flow controller regulates the Lean Solvent Filter flow slipstream to the Electrodialysis Reclaimer via an operator setpoint. After reclamation, this flow combines with the Lean Solvent Filter flow before entering the Absorber. The Filter & Reclaimer Module covers the Activated Carbon Filtration System and the EDR used to remove solvent impurities such as heat-stable salts (HSS), thermal degradation products, and corrosion byproducts. This process maintains the solvent effectiveness at capturing CO and the energetics for regenerating the solvent. 2 The amine solvent must be drained from the plant at shutdown and individual equipment for maintenance activities. The solvent is drained from the equipment by pumping to a minimum level directly or through other vessels to the lean amine solvent storage tank. The remaining amine solution is drained by gravity through the amine waste piping to the amine waste sump. From the sump, the amine solution is pumped through filters to the Amine Solvent Storage Tank. The amine solvent storage tank has been sized to accommodate the amine solution from all plant equipment and piping. The amine waste sump allows the test of the drained amine to ensure that it is of acceptable quality before being pumped into the storage tank. This sump has been sized to accommodate the entire contents of the absorber vessel. If the drained amine solution is unacceptable, it can be pumped directly from the amine waste sump to road tankers for off-site disposal. 3.0 Water Gas Shift Catalyst Disposal The base material of the shift catalyst is iron-chrome, designed for 4-5 years of life span. Through Attachment-2: Solvent Disposal Investigation 5 DE-FE0031937 / 0003 consecutive operations, the blocking of catalyst active sites is occurred by certain elements or compounds on the surface. Continuous monitoring of the effectiveness of the catalyst bed will be ensured through analysis of gas composition as well as lab tests. At the end of life, the deactivated catalyst set needs to be replaced with a new catalyst.
